articles.title: Justiça determina que prefeitura de Boa Vista abrigue indígenas Yanomami em vulnerabilidade | G1
articles.standfirst: Medida atende ação da DPU após a morte de um bebê de 4 meses. A gestão municipal terá prazo de 15 dias e poderá pagar multa de até R$ 100 mil em caso de descumprimento.
articles.summary: Medida atende ação da DPU após a morte de um bebê de 4 meses. A gestão municipal terá prazo de 15 dias e poderá pagar multa de até R$ 100 mil em caso de descumprimento.
articles.body:
Palácio 9 de Julho, sede da prefeitura de Boa Vista — Foto: PMBV/Divulgação

A Justiça Federal determinou que a Prefeitura de Boa Vista alugue, em até 15 dias , um imóvel para abrigar um grupo de 15 a 16 indígenas da etnia Sanumá , subgrupo do povo Yanomami, em situação de extrema vulnerabilidade na capital.

A decisão, da 1ª Vara Federal Cível de Roraima, foi assinada pelo juiz João Bosco Costa Soares da Silva, e atende a um pedido da Defensoria Pública da União (DPU). A determinação prevê que a prefeitura garanta moradia, alimentação e assistência para as famílias, que permanecem na cidade para tratamento de saúde. A ordem deste sábado (14) .

O g1 entrou em contato com a prefeitura de Boa Vista, mas até a última atualização da reportagem não houve retorno.

Em maio deste ano, a Defensoria Pública da União (DPU) em Roraima entrou com uma ação na Justiça Federal p ara garantir direitos básicos a indígenas do povo Yanomami . O pedido foi reforçado após a morte de um bebê, de 4 meses.

De acordo com a ação, a criança morreu por complicações respiratórias associadas às condições precárias de um acampamento improvisado sob lonas plásticas em área sujeita a alagamentos durante o período chuvoso no bairro Jardim Tropical, na zona Oeste da capital.

Relatórios da Fundação Nacional dos Povos Indígenas (Funai) apontam que as famílias dependem de acompanhamento médico e assistência social, o que exige a permanência em Boa Vista.

Pela decisão, a prefeitura deve disponibilizar um imóvel com condições adequadas de moradia, incluindo acesso à água, energia elétrica, banheiros e espaço suficiente para acolher todos os integrantes do grupo .

A casa também deverá ficar em área com acesso a serviços de saúde, assistência social e transporte. Em caso de descumprimento, o município estará sujeito ao pagamento de multa diária de R$ 1 mil, limitada a R$ 100 mil . A decisão prevê ainda a possibilidade de bloqueio de verbas públicas.

A Justiça também determinou que a União, a Funai e o Governo de Roraima prestem apoio no transporte das famílias, forneçam cestas básicas, água potável e kits de higiene, além de garantirem o acompanhamento de saúde por meio da rede de atendimento indígena.

articles.title: Governo Trump propõe mais restrições a trabalhadores estrangeiros | G1
articles.standfirst: Proposta apresentada nesta segunda-feira (16) pelo Departamento do Trabalho define regras mais rígidas para empresas comprovarem que a contratação de estrangeiros não prejudica trabalhadores americanos.
articles.summary: Proposta do Departamento do Trabalho define regras mais rígidas para empresas comprovarem que a contratação de estrangeiros não prejudica trabalhadores americanos.
articles.body:
O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, discursa na Sala de Imprensa da Casa Branca — Foto: REUTERS/Aaron Schwartz

O Departamento do Trabalho dos Estados Unidos propôs, nesta segunda-feira (16), impor novos limites a um programa de vistos que garante a residência permanente para trabalhadores estrangeiros qualificados nos Estados Unidos.

A medida é a mais recente iniciativa do governo do presidente Donald Trump para restringir a imigração legal e tem o potencial de impactar brasileiros selecionados para trabalhar no país.

A proposta será publicada no Registro Federal nesta terça-feira (17) e permanece aberta para comentários públicos por 60 dias antes de poder entrar em vigor e alterar o programa de Certificação Permanente de Trabalho (PERM, na sigla em inglês).

O PERM é utilizado por grandes empresas americanas de tecnologia e firmas de terceirização para obter vistos de residência permanente para funcionários estrangeiros, o que os permite a passar de um status de trabalho temporário para a residência permanente no país.

Antes de contratar um estrangeiro, as empresas precisam comprovar que não há trabalhadores americanos qualificados e disponíveis para a vaga em questão. Além disso, devem indicar que a contratação de alguém do exterior não prejudicará a remuneração ou as condições de trabalho de americanos que ocupam cargos semelhantes.

A reformulação proposta pelo governo Trump, caso entre em vigor, pretende exigir que os empregadores apresentassem provas mais robustas de que a contratação de um estrangeiro não prejudicaria os trabalhadores americanos. A exigência seria estendida a ocupações que, anteriormente, estavam isentas por serem consideradas áreas com escassez de mão de obra — incluindo enfermeiros e cientistas com "habilidade excepcional", segundo as regras.

A medida representa a mais recente tentativa do presidente Donald Trump de restringir o programa e faz parte de um esforço mais amplo de seu governo para reduzir o número de pessoas nascidas no exterior nos Estados Unidos e limitar as vias de acesso à residência e à cidadania locais.

Em outubro deste ano, o governo americano impediu que grandes empresas de tecnologia utilizassem o PERM para reforçar o seu quadro de funcionários — incluindo a fabricante de softwares Adobe, importantes empresas de terceirização de TI e a Microsoft (a maior solicitante de certificações permanentes de trabalho por meio do programa, segundo dados do Departamento do Trabalho americano).

A reformulação proposta pelo Departamento do Trabalho exigiria que os empregadores modernizassem seus métodos de recrutamento interno com trabalhadores americanos para alcançar a "maior base possível de trabalhadores americanos altamente qualificados" — por exemplo, por meio de anúncios de emprego eletrônicos, em vez de impressos.

Além disso, a proposta impediria que as empresas empregadoras americanas buscassem a certificação PERM para trabalhadores estrangeiros caso tenham demitido, nos dois anos anteriores, funcionários americanos em cargos semelhantes.

articles.title: Passe Livre em Manaus: Estudantes podem solicitar 48 créditos | G1
articles.standfirst: Aviso enviado pelo aplicativo Cadê Meu Ônibus informa que os créditos poderão ser utilizados a partir das 4h desta terça-feira (17). Solicitação de até 48 créditos deve ser feita pela internet.
articles.summary: Com o Passe Livre Estudantil Manaus restabelecido pela Justiça, alunos da rede estadual já podem solicitar 48 créditos para transporte pelo site da prefeitura.
articles.body:
Estudantes da rede estadual de ensino de Manaus já podem solicitar os créditos do Passe Livre Estudantil. Um aviso enviado pelo aplicativo Cadê Meu Ônibus na noite desta segunda-feira (16) orienta os alunos a acessar o site da Prefeitura para pedir o benefício.

A liberação ocorre após a Justiça do Amazonas determinar, nesta segunda-feira, o restabelecimento das recargas do Passe Livre Estudantil para alunos da rede estadual que estavam cadastrados como beneficiários em 1º de novembro de 2026.

Segundo a notificação, serão disponibilizados 48 créditos por estudante, que poderão ser utilizados a partir das 4h desta terça-feira (17). A quantidade corresponde a duas passagens por dia durante os 24 dias letivos restantes do ano.

Para solicitar a gratuidade, os estudantes devem acessar o endereço estudantes.manaus.am.gov.br⁠￼ e realizar o procedimento para obter o benefício. O acesso ao transporte gratuito será feito por meio do cartão PassaFácil Estudantil.

Estudantes da rede estadual já podem solicitar 48 créditos do Passe Livre em Manaus. — Foto: Reprodução

A decisão foi proferida pelo juiz Ronnie Frank Torres Stone, da 2ª Vara da Fazenda Pública de Manaus. O magistrado estabeleceu prazo de 24 horas, a contar da intimação, para que o Instituto Municipal de Mobilidade Urbana (IMMU) e o Sindicato das Empresas de Transporte de Passageiros do Estado do Amazonas (Sinetram) adotassem as providências necessárias para a retomada do benefício.

Em caso de descumprimento, foi fixada multa diária de R$ 50 mil para cada instituição.

A decisão também determinou que o Governo do Amazonas repasse R$ 3 milhões ao Sinetram referentes a novembro e outros R$ 3 milhões relativos a dezembro.

Alunos devem estar com dados atualizados para obter Passe Livre Estudantil em Manaus. — Foto: Divulgação

articles.title: Resultado Lotofácil 3831: onze apostas de MT ganham até R$ 2,6 mil | G1
articles.standfirst: Jogos foram registrados em 10 cidades do estado; um deles foi um bolão com 11 cotas.
articles.summary: Jogos foram registrados em 10 cidades do estado; um deles foi um bolão com 11 cotas.
articles.body:
Onze apostas feitas em Mato Grosso acertaram 14 das 15 dezenas do concurso 3831 da Lotofácil , sorteado nesta segunda-feira (16). Os prêmios variam de R$ 1.336,66 a R$ 2.673,32.

Dez apostas eram simples, enquanto uma foi um bolão com 11 cotas, registrado em Sapezal. Também houve uma aposta simples de 16 números, feita em São José dos Quatro Marcos, que recebeu R$ 2.673,32.

Em todo o país, duas apostas acertaram as 15 dezenas e levaram o prêmio principal de R$ 696.133,39 cada. Os jogos foram registrados em Brasília (DF) e Praia Grande (SP). Com isso, o prêmio não acumulou.

Os números sorteados foram: 02 – 04 – 05 – 06 – 09 – 10 – 11 – 13 – 15 – 16 – 17 – 21 – 23 – 24 – 25.

O próximo sorteio será nesta terça-feira (17), com prêmio estimado em R$ 2 milhões.

Para jogar na Lotofácil, é preciso escolher entre 15 e 20 números entre os 25 disponíveis no volante. A aposta com 15 números custa R$ 3,50, e o valor aumenta conforme a quantidade de dezenas marcadas, assim como a chance de acertar.

Também é possível optar pela Surpresinha, modalidade em que o sistema da Caixa Econômica Federal, responsável pela loteria, escolhe os números automaticamente.

São premiadas as apostas que acertam 11, 12, 13, 14 ou 15 números.

articles.title: Aprovação de Trump permanece próxima ao nível mais baixo do mandato | G1
articles.standfirst: Levantamento da Reuters/Ipsos mostra que 66% dos americanos desaprovam o atual mandato, mesmo pico atingido em setembro deste ano. Outros 32% aprovam Trump, um ponto acima do menor número já registrado.
articles.summary: Reuters/Ipsos mostra que 32% dos americanos aprovam o governo Trump 2, variação de 1 ponto em relação ao menor índice do atual mandato, de 31%, registrado em outubro.
articles.body:
O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, desembarca do Air Force One na Base Aérea Conjunta Andrews, após sua visita à Flórida, em Maryland, EUA, em 8 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: Eric Lee/Reuters

A aprovação do presidente Donald Trump permanece próxima ao nível mais baixo de seu mandato, mostra pesquisa Reuters/Ipsos divulgada nesta segunda-feira. Ao todo, 32% dos americanos dizem aprovar o governo Trump 2, enquanto 66% desaprovam.

O menor patamar de popularidade de Trump foi registrado exatamente no levantamento anterior, em outubro, quando 31% dos entrevistados diziam aprovar o presidente.

A variação de 1 ponto percentual para cima, segundo o instituto, mostra um resultado estável ao longo das últimas quatro pesquisas. A margem de erro é de três pontos para mais ou para menos.

Segundo as pesquisas, a popularidade do presidente americano caiu neste ano à medida em que a guerra contra o Irã mexeu nos preços dos combustíveis e atingiu a economia dos americanos. O levantamento mostra que 31% dos americanos defendem a guerra no Irã, segundo a Reuters/Ipsos.

Foram ouvidas 1.521 pessoas adultas em todo o território dos Estados Unidos.

A popularidade de Trump tem sofrido queda desde a sua posse, em janeiro de 2025. Na oportunidade, o presidente era aprovado por 47% dos eleitores entrevistados, enquanto 41% o desaprovavam.

Depois das midterms, eleições de meio de mandato, Trump teve o pior resultado de aprovação. A avaliação negativa sobre a guerra também prejudicou aliados de Trump no Congresso e pode ter interferido no resultado das midterms.

Por outro lado, a aprovação da política migratória do presidente é maior, de 38%. Desde que voltou à Casa Branca, em janeiro de 2025, Trump intensificou as deportações de imigrantes.

No início de novembro, o presidente promoveu Stephen Miller, um dos principais responsáveis pela formulação dessas políticas, ao cargo de novo chefe de gabinete da Casa Branca.

Entre os republicanos, registrados no partido de Trump, 81% apoiam a política migratória do presidente. Em relação ao custo de vida, o índice cai para 50%.

articles.standfirst: TikTok LIVE Fest será realizado em 7 de fevereiro, no Sambódromo do Anhembi, e reunirá cerca de 500 criadores de conteúdo de diferentes países da região.
articles.summary: TikTok LIVE Fest será realizado em 7 de fevereiro, no Sambódromo do Anhembi, e reunirá cerca de 500 criadores de conteúdo de diferentes países da região.
articles.body:
O Camarote Bar Brahma terá programação nos dias 5, 6, 7 e 13 de fevereiro de 2027, no Sambódromo do Anhembi. Os ingressos são vendidos pela plataforma Total Acesso. — Foto: Divulgação/@pridia

O TikTok vai realizar pela primeira vez no Brasil uma premiação para criadores de conteúdo de transmissões ao vivo durante o Carnaval de São Paulo de 2027. O evento chamado TikTok LIVE Fest está marcado para 7 de fevereiro, domingo de Carnaval, no Camarote Bar Brahma, no Sambódromo do Anhembi, na Zona Norte da capital.

O evento deve reunir cerca de 500 criadores de conteúdo de diferentes países da América Latina. A cerimônia será realizada à tarde, antes da abertura do camarote ao público, e terá oito categorias de premiação, além de atrações musicais.

Após a premiação, os convidados poderão acompanhar os desfiles das escolas de samba e os shows de Ludmilla e Mumuzinho no Camarote Bar Brahma.

Segundo a organização, criadores interessados podem se inscrever pelo próprio TikTok para concorrer à oportunidade de participar da experiência.

O Camarote Bar Brahma terá programação nos dias 5, 6, 7 e 13 de fevereiro de 2027, no Sambódromo do Anhembi. A última data corresponde ao Desfile das Campeãs, que reúne as escolas de samba mais bem colocadas na competição do Carnaval paulistano.

📍 Onde? Sambódromo do Anhembi | Av. Olavo Fontoura, 1209, Santana, Zona Norte

articles.title: Papa Leão XIV é atingido por objeto no rosto a caminho de missa | G1
articles.standfirst: Objeto, que aparentava ser um terço, foi arremessado por um fiel e atingiu a região próxima ao olho do pontífice durante despedida de viagem de 12 dias pela América do Sul.
articles.summary: Objeto, que aparentava ser um terço, foi arremessado por um fiel e atingiu a região próxima ao olho do pontífice durante despedida de viagem de 12 dias pela América do Sul.
articles.body:
Na reta final de sua passagem pela América do Sul, nesta segunda-feira (16), o papa Leão XIV foi atingido no rosto por um terço atirado por um fiel quando chegava para uma missa de despedida em Lima, no Peru.

Fotos e vídeos mostram o papa levando a mão ao olho pouco depois de ser atingido, enquanto cumprimentava fiéis a caminho da missa.

Em sua passagem de 12 dias no continente o pontífice chamou a atenção pela habilidade de apanhar objetos jogados pela multidão durante suas aparições públicas.

Ele já conseguiu agarrar bichos de pelúcia, bandeiras e até parou para receber uma pizza oferecida por moradores de Chicago durante uma audiência na Praça de São Pedro, no Vaticano.

Mas não foi a primeira vez que ele falhou ao tentar pegar um objeto lançado em sua direção . Em outra ocasião, durante um evento em Roma, o pontífice pediu desculpas a um cinegrafista do Vaticano após esbarrar nele com a câmera ao tentar agarrar algo jogado em sua direção. Naquela vez, também não conseguiu pegar o objeto.

Aos 71 anos, Leão XIV também é conhecido por jogar tênis e por sua destreza física incomum para a idade.

Papa Leão XIV foi atingido por objeto no rosto. — Foto: REUTERS/Pilar Olivares

Leão XIV é atingido no rosto por objeto a caminho de sua última missa no Peru. — Foto: Reuters

articles.title: Papa Leão XIV se despede da América do Sul depois de viagem de 12 dias a 3 países | G1
articles.standfirst: A Santa Sé estimou que o pontífice reuniu mais de 13 milhões de pessoas ao longo de 50 eventos, entre missas, vigílias, orações, reuniões oficiais e outros encontros mais espontâneos.
articles.summary: A Santa Sé estimou que o pontífice reuniu mais de 13 milhões de pessoas ao longo de 50 eventos, entre missas, vigílias, orações, reuniões oficiais e outros encontros mais espontâneos.
articles.body:
O Papa Leão XIV despediu-se nesta segunda-feira (16) da América do Sul depois de uma viagem de 12 dias a três países.

Doze dias de carinho, muito carinho. E na última volta do papamóvel, um susto. O papa se contorceu e levou a mão ao rosto com expressão de dor. Mas ele se recompôs tão rapidamente que nem mesmo a segurança oficial parece ter notado o incidente. Instantes depois, Leão XIV já estava abençoando um bebê. Segundo a imprensa peruana, o objeto que atingiu o papa foi um terço, atirado por algum fiel , que talvez tenha contado com a agilidade que o papa mostrou dias atrás no Estádio Nacional de Lima ao agarrar um rosário e lançá-lo de volta, abençoado. O fiel, um pouco mais desastrado da missa desta segunda-feira (16), aparentemente está perdoado, porque o papa seguiu como se nada tivesse acontecido - e a multidão também.

Segundo o Vaticano , 2 milhões de fiéis estavam na base aérea de Las Palmas para essa última missa. A Santa Sé estimou que Leão XIV reuniu mais de 13 milhões de pessoas durante a viagem pela América do Sul ao longo de 50 eventos, entre missas, vigílias, orações, reuniões oficiais e outros encontros mais espontâneos.

Papa Leão XIV se despede da América do Sul depois de viagem de 12 dias a 3 países — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

A viagem mais intensa de um papa nas últimas décadas foi um teste de resistência para um senhor de 71 anos recém-operado - tirou um câncer de pulmão há um mês. Leão XIV foi dos ventos gelados do Uruguai ao calor da Amazônia peruana, passando pela chuva e o ar rarefeito da montanha, a 3,7 mil metros de altitude, nos Andes. Três países, 14 cidades, 14 voos, 31 mil quilômetros.

Esses números grandiosos só fazem sentido porque representam pessoas. A América do Sul se mostrou com sede de ouvir as mensagens de paz, diálogo e reconciliação. A viagem de Leão XIV mostrou que, nessa parte do mundo, as palavras do papa são capazes de mover multidões.

Seja diante dos governantes ou dos mais vulneráveis, Leão XIV manteve o tom e o tema. Os discursos tiveram como fio condutor a doutrina social da Igreja. A aplicação das palavras do evangelho ao mundo real e a preservação da dignidade humana e do trabalho. O papa condenou a mentalidade machista e a violência contra as mulheres. Disse que o sangue de lideranças indígenas assassinadas clama a Deus e exige dos homens justiça.

E nesta segunda-feira (16), na homilia, afirmou que os pobres são os únicos que não podem esperar. Os católicos de Lima viveram intensamente essas últimas horas ao lado do papa peruano. Madrugaram na nunciatura apostólica para receber a bênção matinal e se perfilaram no caminho até a base aérea para vê-lo passar.

"Foi muito rápido, mas vimos o suficiente. A paz e a energia que ele transmite é inexplicável", diz uma mulher.

"Graças a Deus que pôde fazer a viagem. Esperamos que siga com saúde e venha muitas vezes mais", afirma outra.

Na base aérea, quem se despediu do papa foi o vice-presidente do Peru , Luis Galarreta. A oposição criticou a presidente Keiko Fujimori por ter embarcado no domingo (15) para uma visita à China e Japão.

Mas que impressão o papa deixou? Ninguém resume o carinho melhor do que a Mia, de 4 anos. Quem passou aqui pela sua rua? O vovozinho. Mais um desafio cumprido na viagem: falar com todas as gerações. Hoje, ela também aprendeu que o vovozinho mora em Roma e que, em algum momento, ele precisa ir para casa.

articles.title: 'We will find you': Iran's chilling warning to US navy officers it blames for Minab school strike
articles.summary: Iran has publicly named and threatened two US navy officers it blames for a Tomahawk missile strike on an elementary school in Minab that killed 168
articles.body: Iran has publicly named and threatened two US navy officers it blames for a Tomahawk missile strike on an elementary school in Minab that killed 168 children. It issued a direct warning to the commanders: "We will find you", according to a Fox News report.The threat came from the Iranian Embassy in South Africa, which took to social media on November 14 to identify the two American officers by name and post their photographs alongside the chilling message.The embassy singled out commander Leigh R Tate, commanding officer assigned to the USS Spruance, and lieutenant commander Jeffrey E York, the warship's executive officer.This was not Tehran's first attempt to put the two officers in the spotlight. In an earlier post on March 28, the Iranian diplomatic mission accused them of directing the Tomahawk missile strikes that hit the elementary school in Minab, Iran, on February 28, killing at least 168 children.It was the same day when US-Israel's combined military operation killed Iran Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei."Remember these two criminals," the embassy had said in that post, before adding, "Don't they have children of their own?"The latest threat comes as the USS Spruance returned to San Diego on Friday after completing a 357-day deployment that included combat operations against Iranian forces.The public naming of the officers has raised fresh security concerns, coming amid an increasingly hostile exchange of warnings between Washington and Tehran.Just a day before the embassy's post, US President Donald Trump had warned Iran of severe consequences if it attempted to assassinate senior American officials.During a November 12 interview with radio personality Hugh Hewitt, Trump was asked how the US would respond if Iran succeeded in killing a senior American official."They will not exist very long, any longer," Trump said.The security concerns have also reached the highest levels of the US administration. articles.title: After stepping away from NBA coaching following a stroke, Gregg Popovich, 77, returned to a San Antonio supermarket with his new wife and paid strangers' grocery bills; one shopper says she cried
articles.summary: A routine grocery run turned into an unforgettable encounter for many San Antonio residents with one of the city’s most adored sports figures.
articles.body: A routine grocery run turned into an unforgettable encounter for many San Antonio residents with one of the city’s most adored sports figures. Legendary former San Antonio Spurs coach Gregg Popovich traded the basketball sidelines for the supermarket checkout counter, surprising customers with an unexpected act of generosity just ahead of Thanksgiving. The 77-year-old basketball executive and his wife Mary Beth paid for customers’ groceries; several shoppers were delighted, and one was particularly touched.A surprising surprise at a San Antonio supermarketAccording to Clutch Points, Popovich and his wife stopped by an H-E-B supermarket on North New Braunfels Avenue in San Antonio, and thrilled shoppers by paying for their purchases. Popovich didn’t just pop in and out; he sat in a chair near the checkout lanes and took care of shoppers’ bills as they came up to the counters.The San Antonio Express News states that It also offered a chance for fans and store workers to meet the basketball icon and get their picture taken with him. Supermarket worker Michael Wiggins shared the unexpected gesture on social media, noting the excitement among customers and staff.Shopper Alice Morales was especially touched by the encounter. She posted a picture with Popovich after he picked up her groceries, and described how the gesture had brought her to tears. Another San Antonio resident Paul Sterling said he was also glad to get the opportunity to meet the former Spurs coach.A tradition of giving in basketballPopovich’s grocery store trip is a reflection of his long-standing commitment to the San Antonio community that goes far beyond his professional basketball accomplishments.He has been a staunch advocate for the San Antonio Food Bank and participated in fundraising events to help food-insecure families, San Antonio Express News reported. A 2024 fundraising dinner tied to these efforts raised enough contributions to feed approximately 1.5 million needy families.He has also been involved with charities for homeless shelters, youth initiatives and the Innocence Project, a non-profit organization that aims to prevent wrongful convictions and exonerate the innocent through DNA-based scientific evidence and legal advocacy.Clutch Points also noted Popovich’s support for causes outside of sports, including efforts to combat childhood hunger. His latest grocery-store gesture was another example of his willingness to make a tangible difference in people’s daily lives.Life after spurs coaching sidelinesThe public appearance follows a major change in Popovich’s professional life. articles.title: British actor Robert Pattinson named as new James Bond
articles.summary: The actor called the studio’s decision a ‘dream come true’.
articles.body:
Robert Pattinson has been named the new James Bond, becoming the seventh actor to assume the role of the iconic British secret agent.

Amazon MGM Studios released a photo of Pattinson in Bond’s signature tuxedo on Monday, confirming the much-anticipated news of who will succeed Daniel Craig. “Identity confirmed,” read a statement posted on Instagram.

Pattinson expressed his gratitude to those at the studio, describing the role as a “dream come true” in a statement.

“James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honor of a lifetime,” he added.

The prolonged casting process to replace Craig, who starred as the super-suave spy in five films since 2006, included British actors Callum Turner, Josh O’Connor and Jack Lowden.

Pattinson shot to international fame playing Edward Cullen in the Twilight series. Since then, he has taken on more independent and fringe roles, most recently in Lance Oppenheim’s Primetime, which starred Pattinson as Chris Hansen from the reality television series To Catch a Predator.

Pattinson has also starred alongside Hollywood superstars Matt Damon and Anne Hathaway in Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey, as well as Matt Reeves’s The Batman. His film, The Drama, alongside co-star Zendaya, was also released this year.

Pattinson’s debut as Bond, currently untitled but widely referred to as “Bond 26,” will be the first 007 film since long-term producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael Wilson stepped back and Amazon took creative control of the franchise, after acquiring the series’ parent company MGM.

Reports have suggested that Pattinson has signed a commitment to make three Bond films.

articles.title: Forensic expert says his analysis of autopsy photos suggests Epstein was killed
articles.summary: Professor Michael Freeman tells BBC Newsnight that he believes the convicted sex offender's injuries are consistent with a homicide.
articles.body:
A forensic expert has said he believes that convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein's death in prison was the result of a homicide, not suicide.

Speaking to BBC Newsnight, Professor Michael Freeman said that after reviewing the New York City medical examiner's file he believes Epstein was strangled, most likely from behind.

The medical examiner who carried out the autopsy concluded in 2019 that Epstein's injuries were consistent with suicide and there was no evidence of the defensive wounds expected if his death had been a homicide.

Epstein was found dead in prison on 10 August 2019 in New York as he awaited trial on sex trafficking charges.

Dr Barbara Sampson, chief medical examiner at the time of Epstein's autopsy, who ruled that Epstein's death was a suicide, has previously said: "I stand firmly behind our determination of the cause and manner of death for Mr. Epstein." The BBC has approached Sampson for further comment.

Freeman has served as a cause-of-death expert to attorneys-general in the US for death in police custody cases, including George Floyd in Minnesota.

He published his research and the New York City medical examiner's files after presenting his findings in London on Monday evening.

Freeman, who did not see the body, based his conclusions on the files and photographs from the examiner's report provided to him by Epstein's brother, Mark Epstein, who has always maintained that his brother was murdered.

Freeman said his analysis is independent and that he was not paid by Mark Epstein. His research has not been peer reviewed.

He told the BBC that he believed there are signs indicating an assault on Epstein, including a deep haemorrhage to his left shoulder and injuries that appear to be consistent to being struck in the face.

Freeman said he believed the evidence was most consistent with strangulation using a ligature and then that same ligature was probably used to suspend the body from the bunk bed.

He said there appeared to be fingernail marks above the ligature mark on Epstein's neck, which "would be consistent with strangulation, particularly from behind. And the attempt by the victim to try to remove the ligature from the neck".

He said "the injuries and the way the body was found don't match up. There's only one remaining explanation then, and that is that the death was as a result of a homicide."

The medical examiner who performed the autopsy at the time told the Department of Justice (DoJ) Office of the Inspector General that Epstein's injuries were more consistent with, and indicative of, a suicide by hanging rather than homicide by strangulation, adding there was no evidence of defensive wounds consistent with what is seen in victims of strangulation.

Freeman said he would have expected in an investigation of a death by hanging in custody for there to be a photograph before the body was taken down.

According to a DoJ investigation into Epstein's time in prison, the guard who found Epstein immediately called for a second colleague to help, lowered Epstein's body to the floor and began attempts to resuscitate him.

Epstein's death came a month after he was briefly placed on suicide watch, the DoJ report said.

When asked who might have killed Epstein if his interpretation of the evidence was correct, Freeman said he had "no idea".

"That is not something I have an opinion about. That isn't any part of any investigation that I've done," he said.

Challenged on whether his views veered into conspiracy theory, Freeman said: "I have the luxury of being able to say, don't take my word for it, let everybody look at it."

"If you think I'm still a conspiracy theorist because I'm looking at something that looks like a strangulation and say, I think it is a strangulation and I don't think it could be a hanging, show me where I got it wrong."

"I'm wide open to that. I'm an academic. I'm quite happy to hear people's theories on things that are informed," he said.

Epstein was convicted in 2008 of soliciting prostitution from a minor, for which he was registered as a sex offender. He escaped a heavy jail sentence as a result of a plea deal.

Eleven years later, Epstein was charged with running a network of underage girls for sex. He was awaiting trial in 2019 when he was found dead at the Metropolitan Correctional Center in New York City.

articles.title: A UK customer bought a £379 laptop online, switched it on and was denied a refund because he had activated Windows 11; after fighting Argos without a lawyer, he won a Court of Appeal ruling two years later
articles.summary: A University of Leicester academic who represented himself in court has won a legal battle against retail giant Argos in the Court of Appeal.
articles.body: A University of Leicester academic who represented himself in court has won a legal battle against retail giant Argos in the Court of Appeal. The ruling protects online shoppers who switch on new laptops to check whether they work before deciding to return them. In a judgment issued on 13 November 2026 in the case of Adodo v Argos Limited, three senior judges unanimously ruled that activating pre-installed Windows 11 software does not remove a buyer's legal right to cancel an online purchase and receive a full refund. The decision ends a two-year legal dispute over a £379 Lenovo IdeaPad laptop. It also orders Argos to return the full purchase price, along with interest calculated from 14 days after the customer first tried to return the laptop in September 2024.How the refund dispute startedAccording to the official judgment published by The National Archives, Dr Ebenezer Adodo ordered a Lenovo IdeaPad 1 laptop bundle from the Argos website on 31 August 2024. He also bought a mouse pad priced at £9.99. The total cost was £388.99, which he paid by card. He selected the retailer's click-and-collect service and chose to collect the items from an Argos desk inside his local Sainsbury's store. Dr Adodo collected the products later that day and took them home. He switched on the laptop to check whether it met the IT requirements for his work. However, he soon found that the computer had compatibility problems with software he used at the University of Leicester. The mouse pad was also too large for his desk.He put both products back into their original boxes and took them to the Sainsbury's collection point on 5 September 2024, just five days after buying them. However, staff refused to refund the laptop. They told him that Argos' terms and conditions did not allow returns once a box had been opened and a laptop had been switched on.The journey through the courtsDr Adodo filed a small claim at Leicester County Court under the Consumer Contracts (Information, Cancellation and Additional Charges) Regulations 2013. These rules give people who buy products online 14 days to cancel their orders without having to explain why. As explained in the Court of Appeal judgment, Argos first argued that click-and-collect purchases did not count as "distance contracts" under the 2013 regulations. A district judge accepted the retailer's argument and dismissed Dr Adodo's claim.Dr Adodo appealed the decision. At the first appeal, His Honour Judge Hedley overturned the earlier ruling. He found that the sales contract had been made online when Argos confirmed the order by email. The fact that the customer collected the products from a store did not change this. Judge Hedley ordered Argos to refund the £9.99 mouse pad but agreed with the retailer over the laptop. Argos relied on a witness statement from Lauren Hunt, a legal assistant at Sainsbury's Group. The retailer argued that switching on the laptop and activating Windows 11 had broken a "digital seal". Judge Hedley accepted this argument and ruled that an exemption under Regulation 28(3)(b) applied. This provision removes the right to cancel a purchase of sealed computer software once the seal has been broken after delivery.Why the Court of Appeal rejected the digital seal argumentDr Adodo decided to challenge the ruling again, this time representing himself against Argos' legal team from Sainsbury's. He took the case to the Court of Appeal in London on 4 November 2026. Lady Justice Andrews, Lady Justice King and Lord Justice Foxton unanimously ruled in his favour and allowed the appeal. In the main judgment, Lady Justice Andrews explained that Dr Adodo had purchased a computer with pre-installed software, not a separate package of sealed computer software."The contract was a contract for the supply of a computer which was preloaded with an operating system to make it functional. It was not a contract for the supply of 'sealed computer software' within the meaning of Regulation 28(3)(b)," Lady Justice Andrews wrote in the ruling. She also warned that accepting Argos' interpretation of the law would seriously weaken consumer protection for people buying electronic products online."Argos' expansive interpretation of that provision would deprive a consumer of the right to cancel almost any contract for the sale of a computer, phone or other electronic gadget which has operating software pre-installed, as most such items do, as soon as the consumer switched on the item and set the software running. Given that many items of that nature are bought online, that would seriously undermine the protection afforded to consumers by the Regulations," the judgment noted.What the ruling means for shoppers and retailersLegal analysts at Solicitor News and Home of Direct Commerce noted that the decision confirms that click-and-collect purchases carry the same 14-day cancellation rights as products delivered directly to a customer's home. The Court of Appeal also explained that customers shopping in physical stores are allowed to inspect and test display products before buying them. Online shoppers should have a similar opportunity to check the products they receive.Under Regulation 34 of the 2013 rules, retailers can reduce a refund if a customer handles a product beyond what is necessary to check its nature, features and how it works. This allows businesses to deduct an amount if the product has lost value because of excessive handling. However, Lady Justice Andrews pointed out that Argos had not provided evidence showing that switching on the laptop had reduced its value. The retailer had also failed to prove that it had faced any specific costs to reset the computer.The ruling could lead retailers across the UK to review their return policies, particularly rules that automatically reject refunds for electronics bought online simply because customers have opened the packaging or switched on the device. The decision makes clear that activating pre-installed software does not, by itself, remove a shopper's legal right to cancel an online computer purchase within the 14-day cooling-off period.You use AI every day. articles.title: A woman challenged her late mother-in-law’s will after it left the family home to her grandson; the High Court ruled it invalid after finding that one of the two witnesses had not signed it
articles.summary: A woman has challenged her late mother-in-law’s will after a High Court judge found that one of the two people named as witnesses had not signed the
articles.body: A woman has challenged her late mother-in-law’s will after a High Court judge found that one of the two people named as witnesses had not signed the document. Alicia Lopez Batiller, the estranged wife of Dorothy May Edwards’ son, Clive Edwards, challenged the will dated 24 December 2012. The document left Dorothy’s remaining estate, mainly her home in Flintshire, to her grandson, Steven Beales. This differed from an earlier will made in August 2012, which divided her remaining estate equally between her daughter, Valerie Beales, and son, Clive Edwards.According to the High Court judgment in Alicia Lopez Batiller v Clive Edwards & Ors [2026] EWHC 2086 (Ch), Alicia Lopez Batiller challenged the December 2012 will on grounds including forgery, undue influence and lack of due execution.How did Dorothy’s December 2012 will differ from her earlier oneDorothy’s earlier will was dated 20 August 2012 and had been professionally drawn up by Legal & Contract Services Ltd. It left her residuary estate equally to her daughter, Valerie Beales, and her son, Clive Edwards. No challenge was made to that document.The later will, dated 24 December 2012, instead left the residuary estate to Steven Beales, Valerie’s son and Dorothy’s grandson. The estate essentially comprised Hillcrest Leeswood, the property in Flintshire where Alicia Lopez Batiller was living under a family court occupation order.Dorothy died in 2017, but probate for the December 2012 will was not granted until January 2024. Alicia subsequently challenged its validity in the High Court.Family agreement placed Dorothy’s estate in her grandson’s nameClive told the court that the December 2012 will was signed at Hillcrest on Christmas Eve. He said his sister, Valerie, was terminally ill at that time and wanted to put everything in order. According to him, she had prepared the draft after discussions involving him and Steven, and the family had agreed that Steven would inherit the estate while Dorothy and the parties could continue living at Hillcrest.He recalled being present when his mother signed it, along with his sister, Lucille Ingram, and Stuart Youd. He said he saw Ingram sign the document but did not see Youd do so. Clive also told the court that his sister initially kept the will before Youd handed it to him a few years later.He stored it in a safe at the family home, Hillcrest, but moved it around 2017 because he feared Alicia might gain access to it. He then hid the document in a gap between wardrobes at the property. He applied for probate only when the issue arose during family proceedings.What made Dorothy’s signature on the 2012 will suspiciousBoth parties instructed handwriting experts, who submitted reports and a joint statement to the court. They agreed that Dorothy’s known signatures varied considerably. They also noted that the letter ‘M’ in her middle name, May, was formed differently in the disputed December 2012 will compared with her earlier signatures. Adam Brand, the expert instructed by Alicia Lopez Batiller (claimant), considered it probable that Dorothy had not signed the document. He said the differences in letter spacing, the formation of the capital ‘M’ and the letter ‘d’ were significant.He suggested that Clive might have written the signature, pointing out that his handwriting closely resembled his late mother’s. Clive denied this, explaining that she had taught him to write.Ruth Myers, the expert instructed by Clive, maintained that the disputed signature was written by the same person as Dorothy’s known signatures. She questioned why a forger would not have copied the letter ‘M’ more closely if the signature had been fabricated. However, she did not provide an opinion on the disputed signature of the second witness, Stuart Youd.What evidence led the judge to question the will’s witnessesJudge Jarman KC said the expert evidence about Dorothy’s signature was divided. However, he described the evidence concerning Youd’s signature as strong and persuasive. The judge concluded, on the balance of probabilities, that Youd had not signed the December 2012 will.The December 2012 will purportedly carried Dorothy’s signature and named Lucille Ingram, Clive’s cousin, and Stuart Youd, Valerie’s partner, as witnesses. It referred to Valerie by her married name, although she had not yet married Youd when the document was signed. The couple married the following month. Valerie died later in 2013. Both named witnesses died in 2020, leaving Clive as the only person who could give direct evidence about the signing of the will and what happened to it afterwards.The judge also considered evidence from Stuart Youd’s two daughters, Kerry Roberts and Anna Edwards, who gave their statements through video link. Kerry said she had visited her father at his home on Christmas Eve 2012 and stayed until late afternoon. She recalled that he had not mentioned visiting Dorothy Edwards at Hillcrest that day. Anna said she had telephoned her father on the same day and he had not mentioned any plans to leave the house.The judge accepted their evidence. Under Section 9(c) of the Wills Act 1837, two witnesses were required for a will to be validly executed. The judge ruled that the will dated 24 December 2012 was invalid because it had not been properly witnessed.Disclaimer: This article is based on the High Court judgment in Alicia Lopez Batiller v Clive Edwards & Ors [2026] EWHC 2086 (Ch). The Times of India has not independently verified the disputed claims about the will, the alleged forgery, or the circumstances surrounding its signing. The findings mentioned in this article reflect the court's judgment.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Pope Leo’s return to Latin America reveals the missionary message of his papacy
articles.summary: His visit to South America will go down as one of the lasting images of his papacy. It also sends message to the wider church: that it is the people on the margins who must take priority.
articles.body: Pope Leo XIV’s visit to South America will go down as one of the lasting images of his papacy. He drew massive crowds and there was an emotional outpouring over his return to Peru just weeks after having undergone lung cancer surgery. Leo XIV’s trip has dispelled, for now, any lingering questions about his health, as he kept up a dizzying schedule of events over the 12-day visit with dozens of speeches and events. It also showed how comfortable Leo has been in a continent where he spent a large chunk of his adult life. A pope with dual identities The pope was visibly moved when he sang the Peruvian national anthem on his arrival in Lima and was seen wiping away tears during a gathering of young people in the national stadium. Outside of the Vatican, and in a place he calls home, the pope seemed relaxed and far less scripted. He would frequently speak off-the-cuff to the people who gathered outside the different papal embassies where he stayed during his trip. He was even able to stay in his former home in Chiclayo, at the bishop’s residence in the northern city in Peru where he once served as a bishop. The trip to Peru also highlighted how the Chicago-born pontiff balances dual identities. As we flew out from Rome to Uruguay’s capital Montevideo with Pope Leo XIV, I asked him about his recent decision to cast a vote in the US midterm elections, a decision which surprised some in the Vatican given the pope is a head of state. “I’m proud to be an American,” he replied. “And to exercise the right [to vote].” His latest foreign tour, however, has seen him emphasize his Peruvian identity with people in Peru seeing “Papa Leon” as one of their own. “¡El papa es peruano!” (The Pope is Peruvian) was frequently chanted during his time in the country where he spent around two decades as a missionary and bishop. When Rev. Robert Prevost was appointed Bishop of Chiclayo it was a requirement he became a citizen, and the pope continues to hold citizenship. “The Peruvian people are my people too,” he said during the final mass of his tour at Las Palmas Airbase in Lima, before boarding a plane to Rome on Monday. His decision to vote in the US midterms, and make it known, sent a message about the importance of voting, and his support for democracy. He emphasized this message in Argentina, with the pope urging President Javier Milei to safeguard democracy and to adopt a “careful use of words.” It’s a message with wider resonance in Latin America, where the pope has witnessed firsthand the fragility of democracy. Arriving in Peru, he was greeted by President Keiko Fujimori, the daughter of the disgraced late President Alberto Fujimori, who was convicted of authorizing the operation of a death squad in his country. As a missionary in Peru, he witnessed then President Alberto Fujimori dissolve congress and suspend the constitution along with grave human rights violations. In 2017, Prevost criticized Alberto Fujimori’s pardon, saying that the former president’s apology had been too generic for the victims of his regime. While Catholic Church in the past has been skeptical and hostile to democracy, the first American pope is becoming one of its most prominent defenders. Enormous crowds Leo drew huge crowds during his time in South America. More than 12 million people were estimated to have turned out for papal events and masses in Uruguay, Argentina and Peru. In the Argentine capital Buenos Aires, he presided over the largest Mass of his pontificate with around 2.5 million people in attendance, and 3 million lined the streets of the Peruvian city of Lima for his return, according to Vatican estimates provided by local authorities. The most emotional welcome came on Friday in the northern Peruvian city of Chiclayo, a commercial center for the region that is unevenly developed. The warmth of its residents was on full display when they gave a hero’s welcome to their former bishop who returned to them as pope. Pope-fever took over the city with banners and posters of Leo plastered everywhere, as well as the sale of a special “papaleta” pope ice cream in a Leo XIV shaped figure. One restaurant, named Papa Johns, announced it would temporarily re-name itself “Johns,” as there “is only one papa” in town that week. The crowd was in a celebratory mood throughout, frequently chanting “¡El papa es chiclayano” (The pope is Chiclayan) and clambering up on railings near his residence to try and catch a glimpse of the man they know as “Padre Roberto.” Overcoming health problems Being back in a place he knows so well, appeared to give the pope a sense of vitality. Despite his recent surgery, he showed no signs of slowing down or needing to take any breaks. As a Chicago south-sider, he comes from a place known for its work ethic and resilience, or in the words of Sean Connery in the 1987 movie “The Untouchables”: “That’s the Chicago way.” Still, to pull off the visit so soon after his surgery was telling and sends a message to those in the Vatican and beyond that he is fit and well. He managed his trip to high-altitude Cusco, which is more than 11,000 feet above sea level, where he met indigenous peoples and led services. And for the journalists traveling with him, it was hard to keep up with the relentless pace. After a cancer diagnosis, nothing is guaranteed, and the pope pointedly said that he was still “overcoming” his illness during the Mass on the outskirts of Chiclayo last week. “Thank you for your affection, support and prayers, especially for my health during this time of trial which, with God’s help, I am overcoming,” the 71-year-old pontiff said. A missionary pope While in Peru, Leo went back to his missionary roots. The last two popes have been bishops in Latin America, and both have them have emphasized the importance of a church that goes out of its comfort zone. Pope Francis, the first Argentinian pope, said he preferred that church “which is bruised, hurting and dirty because it has been out on the streets” rather than a church which unhealthily clinging onto its security. Leo has borne that out, becoming a missionary in Peru at the age of 30. When he lived there, he loved to drive, and as a bishop he would make the journey across the rugged, winding mountain roads in the Peruvian Andes. While his trip last week saw a change to his pace — where he traversed the length of the country on Sunday –– there was little deviation from his decades-long commitment to his Peruvian flock. He is the first pope in centuries to have served as a foreign missionary before his election, and this trip emphasized how Leo still has the missionary spirit and feels most comfortable as a pastor among his people in the remote towns of the Andes. It is also sending a message to the wider church: that it is the people on the margins who must take priority. With his return to Peru, the pope has decided to visit Chiclayo ahead of Chicago. But the scenes that greeted Leo XIV during his time in Latin America are a taster of what a return trip to the United States might look.

articles.summary: An Israeli government without PM Netanyahu may be close, but a government without his politics is far less certain.
articles.body:
As the long and complex negotiations to form Israel’s next government drag on, hopes are high that former military chief Gadi Eisenkot will be able to form a coalition that marks a break from the far-right and divisive politics of the previous administration.

The coalition brought together by the now-caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu brought figures from Israel’s far right into government. Beyond the genocidal war on Gaza following the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attack on Israel, and repeated military strikes against neighbouring countries, the government sought to weaken judicial oversight and pursued an aggressive policy of illegal settlement expansion in the occupied West Bank. There, settler pogroms against Palestinian communities have continued with near impunity.

“Likud sits further to the right than most conservative parties in Europe. Although historically it was thought of as something like the Conservative Party, today it looks like something of a far-right party,” said Roi Zur, an Israeli academic at the University of Essex, who has researched the comparison between Israeli parties and their international equivalents.

In contrast, Eisenkot and his opposition bloc have said that they will repeal the judicial overhaul legislation introduced by Netanyahu, establishing a state commission of inquiry into the security failings ahead of the October 7 attack, and ending the draft exemption offered to many ultra-Orthodox youth in defiance of a 2024 ruling by the Supreme Court.

But will a new government under Eisenkot – made up of a number of right-wing figures – really be any different from what has come before?

What parties and politicians are likely to sit in government with Eisenkot?

As it stands, before any fresh alliances are brokered, there are five main political leaders of the opposition bloc.

Its leader, Eisenkot, the leader of the Yashar Party, is generally regarded as a centrist security hawk.

Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid of the B’Yachad Party are considered right-wing and centre-liberal, respectively.

Avigdor Lieberman, the head of Yisrael Beiteinu, is secular and right-wing, while Yair Golan of the Democrats sits as the sole outlier on the left.

What do we know about Eisenkot’s politics?

Many observers regard Eisenkot’s politics as difficult to read.

While he has been broadly supportive of the genocidal war on Gaza, in which more than 74,600 Palestinians have been killed, and attacks on countries across the region, including the current war on Iran, little is known of his domestic politics.

His Yashar Party’s economic platform points towards a broadly pro-market approach, prioritising tax cuts over wealth redistribution.

On security, there is less ambiguity. Eisenkot is the architect of the Dahiya doctrine, an Israeli military strategy that calls for overwhelming force against areas from which Israel comes under attack.

Eisenkot warned in 2008 that Israel’s destruction of large parts of southern Beirut’s Dahiya area during the 2006 war on Lebanon “will happen in every village from which fire is launched toward Israel”. In March, he said the doctrine should again be used in Lebanon, noting it had “never been more relevant”.

Eisenkot has also firmly rejected the establishment of a Palestinian state, and supports the continued existence of illegal settlements in the West Bank, even though he has pledged to tackle settler violence.

How about the others in Eisenkot’s bloc?

The bloc may be viewed internationally as more moderate than Netanyahu, but its members also largely adopt right-wing positions towards Palestinians.

Bennett, a former settler council chief, opposes Palestinian statehood and has previously said that he favours annexing 60 percent of the West Bank. His political partner, Lapid, backs a two-state solution, but without any firm details, and then only in the long term.

Netanyahu’s former ally and now one of his fiercest critics, Lieberman has been vocal in his support of the expansion of illegal settlements.

Both Bennett and Lieberman have made incendiary comments about Palestinians. Bennett defended cutting off water and electricity to Palestinians in Gaza in October 2023, while Lieberman said in December 2023 that there were “no innocents in Gaza”.

Bennett and Lapid have led a government in the past: their 2021 coalition included the United Arab List (Ra’am), a party representing Palestinian citizens of Israel. But it eventually collapsed the next year, partly because it was split over privileges settlers received in the West Bank.

However, while something can be gleaned from Bennett and Lapid’s time in office, how the contrasting visions of the left-wing Golan and the right-wing Lieberman will work in the same coalition remains to be seen.

“Golan and the party he is heading, the Democrats, are a merger of two Zionist left-wing parties, the centre-left Labour and the harder-left Meretz,” said Or Tuttnauer, interim professor at the University of Mannheim, who has studied the Israeli opposition. “The party holds liberal, progressive, dovish, secular positions.”

In contrast, Tuttnauer said, Lieberman and his right-wing Yisrael Beiteinu party sought to define themselves against others holding similar positions through both his emphasis on secularism and fierce opposition to Netanyahu.

Can the potential new coalition be considered more liberal in any way?

Any country that depends on the military occupation of roughly 7,252 square kilometres (2,800 square miles) of Palestinian and Syrian territory, and rules over some 5.5 million Palestinians who have no vote in the state that controls them, is unlikely to be considered progressive or liberal.

Beyond its foreign policy, however, Israel’s society has been shifting steadily to the right, a trend that polling suggests accelerated sharply following the October 7, 2023 attack.

“Many people have pinned their hopes on Netanyahu leaving, imagining that a moderate or even progressive government would follow,” HA Hellyer of the Royal United Services Institute said. “But the problem was never just Netanyahu. His absence would only expose how far the rest of the Israeli political spectrum, including much of the opposition, shares the same positions on occupation and Palestinian rights.”

“It will take years before Israelis, the public and not just their leaders, accept the case for withdrawing from Gaza, the occupied West Bank, or even Syria and southern Lebanon,” Hellyer said. “Ending the occupation and dismantling apartheid all entail recognising that these things have happened first.”

articles.title: 'This was a miracle': Cruise passengers describe frantic escape as tanker strikes ship
articles.summary: Two American Heritage cruise passengers described the frightening moment they saw the Atlantic Asphalt tanker heading straight for their dining room window.
articles.body: Two cruise passengers thought something looked wrong outside the window of their ship. Moments later, they were running for their lives. Tamara Carrasco and Stephanie Chiappetta were aboard the American Heritage when the Atlantic Asphalt tanker struck the docked river cruise ship on the Mississippi River in New Orleans on Friday, Nov. 13. There were 191 passengers and crew members sailing on the American Heritage, and roughly 100 people ended up in the river as the vessel capsized after the collision, as Fox News Digital previously reported. NEW ORLEANS CRUISE SHIP DISASTER TIMELINE REVEALS CRUISE SHIP'S TROUBLED PAST AND FRANTIC FINAL MINUTES Carrasco and Chiappetta recalled the frightening moments leading up to the crash during an appearance on "America's Newsroom." The women were sitting in the dining room looking out at the water when they noticed the tanker's anchor going down. Chiappetta soon realized the ship appeared to be heading directly toward them. "Stephanie said, 'It's going to hit us. It's coming right at us,'" Carrasco recalled. "I kept watching, hoping that it would veer away." As the tanker drew closer, Chiappetta told Carrasco they needed to leave. A waiter also began warning passengers to get out of the glass-filled dining room. Carrasco said people began yelling for everyone to leave, prompting the women to run. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER "When it came time to run, it was, 'Where do I go that I'm not gonna die?' Because it was that close at that point," she said. Investigators are now piecing together what happened aboard the tanker in the minutes before impact. The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) recovered the Atlantic Asphalt's voyage data recorder, which captured about nine hours of information from the vessel, "America’s Newsroom" reported. Preliminary information indicates the tanker experienced a steering problem that left its rudder turned to the right before it struck the American Heritage at about 12:28 p.m., senior marine investigator Bart Barnum with the NTSB said during a Sunday press briefing. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES The recorder captured sounds from the roughly two minutes between the steering problem and the collision, including the ship's whistle, radio warnings and calls for assistance, orders to drop the anchors and emergency commands, Barnum said. As passengers rushed to safety, Chiappetta said the crew relied on safety training to help people evacuate. "The staff was amazing," she said. "They have a routine. They've done their drills. We were so blessed." TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "This was a miracle," Carrasco added. No fatalities were reported in the collision. Thirty-two people, however, were injured, according to reports. The American Heritage's captain was injured but remained on board the ship until all passengers and crew were accounted for — becoming the last person to leave the vessel, New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno said, as Fox News Digital previously reported. The NTSB has not yet determined the cause of the collision. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Investigators are continuing to review the voyage recorder, other electronic evidence and the tanker's maintenance and mechanical history. Brittany Miller of Fox News Digital contributed reporting.

articles.title: California braces for its most widespread atmospheric river of the season
articles.summary: Flooding rain, mountain snow and gusty winds will threaten most of California as an incoming storm pulls in the most widespread atmospheric river of the season.
articles.body: Flooding rain, heavy mountain snow and gusty winds will threaten most of California this week as an incoming storm pulls in the most widespread atmospheric river of the season. 🌧️ Track the storm in the CNN Weather app An atmospheric river is pretty much what it sounds like: a long, narrow plume of moisture that can flow thousands of miles, like a fire hose in the sky. California is likely to see plenty more atmospheric river-fueled storms in the weeks and months to come as a potentially historic super El Niño boosts the state’s odds of a wet winter. The storm will spread across California by Wednesday and linger through Thursday, with the threat of flooding rainfall stretching from the Bay Area down to Los Angeles and San Diego. The National Weather Service in Los Angeles calls the coming system “the first storm of the season with truly widespread moderate to heavy rain and high elevation mountain snow.” Northern California and the Pacific Northwest have already been battered by a series of storms over the weekend into Monday. Massive waves pounded much of the Pacific Coast, damaging Monterey Bay’s historic Capitola Wharf, while floodwater as deep as 2 feet inundated Bay Area highways, and wind gusts up to 64 mph buffeted Sonoma County. Here’s what to expect this week. Heavy rain raises flooding concerns across the state Heavy downpours will arrive across the Bay Area and Central Coast beginning early Wednesday morning. These areas are under a Level 2 of 4 risk for flooding rain Wednesday, according to the Weather Prediction Center. Rainfall totals of 1 to 2 inches are forecast across much of the region, with 3 to 4 inches possible in spots, especially in the coastal mountain ranges. Much of the heaviest rain could fall in just three to six hours as the storm’s front moves through. Periods of showers will persist in the wake of that heavier burst through Thursday. The combination of intense downpours and increasingly saturated ground from the back-to-back storms could lead to flooding on roads. Farther inland, at least 1 inch of rain is likely across the Sacramento Valley and nearby Sierra Nevada foothills, with 2 inches or more possible in some areas Wednesday and Thursday. The flooding rain threat will spread to Los Angeles, San Diego and surrounding mountain areas by late Wednesday night into Thursday morning. Parts of Southern California, including those metros, are under a Level 2 of 4 risk of flooding rain Thursday, according to the Weather Prediction Center. Rainfall totals of 1 to 3 inches are possible across portions of Southern California with locally higher amounts of 3 to 5 inches possible on some mountain slopes. The biggest punch of heavy rain will be within a four-to-eight-hour window from late Wednesday night through Thursday morning, the National Weather Service in Los Angeles said. Flooding is possible in urban areas and rockslides could tumble down on canyon roads. Recently burned areas could also be prone to flooding and debris flows, especially if thunderstorms bring short bursts of heavier rain. Burned ground can’t absorb as much water and intense rainfall rates can also loosen up soil, making it easier for rain to carry it downhill. Feet of snow and strong winds expected Cold air is also accompanying this storm, and winter storm watches and warnings are posted for heavy snow in the Sierra Nevada, which, while beneficial for ski resorts, will cause major travel headaches. Mountain passes like Interstate 80 through Donner Pass will see dangerous travel conditions beginning Wednesday with snow falling at rates of 1 to 2 inches per hour alongside gusty winds. Snow could accumulate at elevations as low as 4,000 feet, with at least 2 feet likely in some mountain locations above 5,000 feet through Thursday night. A few areas could receive 3 feet or more. Strong winds will also accompany the storm, with gusts of 30 to 45 mph possible in parts of the Bay Area and elsewhere in interior Northern California on Wednesday and Thursday. That could be strong enough to down a few trees and cause scattered power outages.

articles.title: Netanyahu’s opponents demand investigation after report alleges that his staff tried to influence elections
articles.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is facing calls from lawmakers for an investigation following a report that alleged that a member of his staff provided information to police against Arab citizens in an attempt to influence last month’s elections. The claims, which Netanyahu’s office denies, were made on an Israeli TV news show this weekend.
articles.body: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is facing calls from lawmakers for an investigation following a report that alleged that a member of his staff provided information to police against Arab citizens in an attempt to influence last month’s elections. The claims, which Netanyahu’s office denies, were made on an Israeli TV news show this weekend. The controversy centers on the widely publicized arrest of three activists from the Arab party Raam in southern Israel early on the morning of the October 27 election over an alleged cash-for-votes scheme. Throughout the day, Netanyahu and his Likud party repeatedly amplified the arrests to mobilize their own voters, alleging Raam was trying to “steal the elections.” Courts later rejected police requests to keep the suspects in custody, saying that the arrests were carried out without a valid search or arrest warrant. All suspects have since then been released. According to an investigation by Channel 12’s “Uvda,” the allegation originated in Netanyahu’s office. The day before the elections, the report alleges, Netanyahu’s chief of staff, Ido Norden, bypassed standard reporting channels and personally contacted the police commissioner to alert him about the activists, passing on information. Norden allegedly referred police to a separate source who was said to hold information about the activists. But the source was a former employee of the Prime Minister’s Office, the report said. Based on Norden’s complaint and the information provided by the former employee, police carried out the arrests on election day, the report alleged. On Monday evening, Israel’s Attorney General said she would hold a discussion on the transfer of information from the Prime Minister’s Office to the police. “As part of the discussion, all aspects relating to the matter will be examined,” the Attorney General’s spokesperson said in a statement. Netanyahu’s office strongly denied the Channel 12 report, saying it was “false and grounds for libel,” but confirmed that Nordan had passed information to the police. “Criminal information reached Chief of Staff Ido Norden, he fulfilled his duty as expected of any law-abiding citizen and connected that person to the police,” his office said in a statement Sunday evening. Norden learned on the morning of the elections that a person “was indeed caught with tens of thousands of shekels in cash and Raam slips,” the statement continued, referring to a suspect who had already been released. In a statement, Israel Police said it would examine “the decision-making processes, the chain of reporting, the working interfaces between the relevant police units, and the division of responsibility” related to the allegations in the Channel 12 report. “All police actions, including the operation carried out on election morning, were taken out of commitment and transparency toward the public, and with the aim of protecting the integrity of the elections,” police said. On Monday evening, the Attorney General requested a pause in this examination until there is a decision “on the appropriate format for the inquiry.” The main opposition party is calling for an immediate investigation. Gadi Eisenkot, the leader of Yashar and a candidate to replace Netanyahu as prime minister, said the conduct of Netanyahu and his circle is “a tangible, direct and immediate threat to Israeli democracy,” warning that “as long as Netanyahu is in office, there will be no more fair and proper elections in Israel.” Two Arab parties that saw record voter turnout in the elections also demanded an immediate criminal investigation. “The arrest of our activists in the Negev on the morning of the elections and the attempt to silence Arab Knesset members, if proven, is a direct attack on the integrity of the elections and the will of the voters,” Raam said in a statement, referring to Israel’s parliament. The Joint List called to establish an independent commission of inquiry – the state’s highest investigative body – and suspend all involved police and Shin Bet officials. “Netanyahu tried to steal our vote, but our vote is what will bring him down. His place is not in the Prime Minister’s Office, but in the interrogation room and before the court,” the party said in a statement. Since losing his parliamentary majority in the October 27 vote, Netanyahu and his allies have raised various allegations against the Arab parties, accusing them of bribery, foreign funding, and fraud. David Zini, the director of the Shin Bet domestic security service and a Netanyahu loyalist, has pressed to investigate Arab politicians over allegations of foreign interference, but so far hasn’t presented any public evidence to support the allegations against them. According to the Channel 12 report, Zini demanded to wiretap five Arab lawmakers before election day. The request was refused at the last minute by the attorney general because he did not present any evidence to back his request, Channel 12 reported. In a statement, the Shin Bet said it carried out “various activities in accordance with its powers under the law.” Avigdor Liberman, the leader of the Yisrael Beitenu party and the interim chair of the crucial Knesset Foreign Affairs and Defense Committee, said on Monday that he would summon the Shin Bet and police chiefs to discuss alleged foreign interference attempts in the election.

Netanyahu called on Israelis to vote "the right way" on October 27 as he cast his ballot in Jerusalem, facing a close-fought race in a pivotal general election.
